title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 55
paragraphs: When the herald came to the Lacedaemonians, he saw they were still in their place and their leaders had come to strife with one another. For although Euryanax and Pausanias both urged Amompharetos not to risk remaining behind with his men, alone of all the Lacedaemonians, they did not persuade him at all, and at last they had come to outright strife. Meanwhile the Athenian herald had arrived and was standing beside them. Amompharetos, in his disputing, took up a rock in both hands and set it at Pausanias's feet, saying that with this pebble he cast his vote not to flee from the strangers — meaning the barbarians. Pausanias, calling him a madman and out of his senses, bade the Athenian herald — who was asking what he had been charged to ask — be told the state of their affairs; and at the same time he asked the Athenians to come toward the Lacedaemonians and to do the same as they did regarding the retreat.
